address: Nuggets Crossing Courtyard, 6 Kosciuszko Road, Jindabyne NSW 2627
long_description: Sundance Bakehouse is the Snowy Mountains institution that skiers line up for before heading to the mountain. Opening at 5:30am daily – earlier than any other food outlet in Jindabyne – it serves freshly baked pies, pastries, gourmet sandwiches, rolls, slices and seriously good coffee. The Jindabyne flagship is in Nuggets Crossing Courtyard; sister stores open in winter at Bullocks Flat Skitube terminal and Perisher Valley. Famous locally for its pies and its early-morning ritual.
name: Sundance Bakehouse
short_description: Cult Jindabyne bakery open from 5:30am – the earliest breakfast stop in town for ski-day mornings.
signature_dishes: freshly baked pies | pastries | gourmet sandwiches and rolls | slices | takeaway coffee

address: Shop 3, Nuggets Crossing Shopping Centre, 13 Kalkite Street, Jindabyne NSW 2627
long_description: Nimmitabel Bakery has been using traditional baking methods since 1950 in the heritage town of Nimmitabel. Its Jindabyne outpost in Nuggets Crossing Shopping Centre has a cosy fireplace, making it an ideal morning stop before or after the mountain. Signature items include brekky wraps, homemade pies, and picnic hampers filled with pastries and snacks. Coffee is made with Seven Miles' Black Mountain beans.
name: Nimmitabel Bakery
short_description: Traditional bakery founded in 1950, now with a cosy Jindabyne outpost featuring a fireplace and Seven Miles coffee.
signature_dishes: brekky wrap | homemade pie | picnic hampers | Seven Miles Black Mountain coffee

long_description: Birchwood is consistently rated the best cafe in Jindabyne for brunch and lunch. The menu spans granola bowls, avo on toast, Turkish eggs, B&E rolls, creamy soups, poke bowls and burgers, with alcohol available from 10am. Their standout ski-day Lunch Packs (sandwich, juice, veggie sticks, fruit, sweet slice) make packing mountain food effortless. Single O beans coffee and house-made kombucha complete the offering. Open 7am–2pm daily.
name: Birchwood
short_description: Best brunch spot in Jindabyne – modern Australian fusion cafe on Gippsland St with Single O coffee and all-day ski-day lunch packs.
signature_dishes: Turkish eggs | avo on toast | B&E roll | poke bowl | burger | ski-day Lunch Packs | Single O coffee

address: 49 Kosciuszko Road (Snowy Region Visitor Centre), Jindabyne NSW 2627
long_description: Parc Cafe sits inside the Snowy Region Visitor Centre on Kosciuszko Road, making it the ideal first stop before collecting national park day passes. Open from 6:30am Monday–Saturday and 8am Sundays, it serves Madding Crowd coffee, organic juices, smoothies, big brekkies, burritos, sambos and wraps. Local Jindabyne Brewing Co beers and Shut the Gate wines are also on tap. Live music runs in summer and the cafe is available for private functions in the evening.
name: Parc Cafe
short_description: All-day cafe at the Snowy Region Visitor Centre open from 6:30am – one of the earliest coffee stops before heading to the mountain.
signature_dishes: big brekkie | burritos | wraps | Madding Crowd coffee | local craft beer

address: Corner of Wollondibby Road and The Alpine Way, Crackenback NSW 2627
long_description: Located on the Alpine Way between Jindabyne and Thredbo, Wildbrumby is the Snowy Mountains' most distinctive dining destination. The Stillhouse Cafe sits next to working distillery stills and offers a Continental-influenced menu featuring the distillery's signature gins, schnapps, glühwein and vodka in every drink. The organic raspberry patch, sculpture garden and outdoor terrace make it an exceptional apres-ski detour on the drive back from Thredbo. Reservations recommended on weekends. Famous locally as 'the schnapps place.'
name: Wildbrumby Distillery & Cafe (Stillhouse Cafe)
short_description: Famous for its Snowy Mountains schnapps, gin and vodka – distillery cafe with Austrian-influenced menu, open Thu–Mon.
signature_dishes: schnapps (raspberry, elderflower, pear) | gin and tonics with local botanicals | glühwein | daily-changing menu with local produce

cuisine: pub food | modern Australian | pizza | burgers | craft beer
long_description: The Banjo Paterson Inn is Jindabyne's quintessential apres-ski hub. Clancy's Brasserie serves pub classics including chicken schnitzel, Caesar salad, grilled Snowy River trout and a full grill selection. The Overflow is the more casual outlet, specialising in burgers and pizzas. Three bars – Musters Bar with outdoor terrace views of Lake Jindabyne, the sports bar and the Kosciuszko Brewhouse – mean there's always somewhere to watch the game or enjoy a Kosciuszko Pale Ale. Live music and nightly events run year-round.
name: The Banjo Paterson Inn – Clancy's Brasserie & The Overflow
short_description: Jindabyne's best-known pub complex with two restaurants, three bars and the Kosciuszko Brewhouse pouring craft ales on-site.
signature_dishes: Snowy River trout | chicken schnitzel | Kosciuszko Pale Ale | burgers (The Overflow) | pizza (The Overflow)

long_description: The Lake Jindabyne Hotel Bistro is widely regarded as serving the best pub food in the Snowy Mountains. The menu is classic Australian pub fare – generous steaks, schnitzels, lamb shanks, pork belly, pasta – but executed with care and at pub prices. The outdoor veranda with sweeping lake views and indoor sports bar make it great year-round, and the self-serve sauce station adds a casual, no-fuss vibe. A favourite for locals and visitors alike. 300-seat capacity with waterfront seating.
name: Lake Jindabyne Hotel Bistro
short_description: Lakefront pub bistro famous for legendary steaks, generous serves and panoramic lake views – a Jindabyne local institution.
signature_dishes: 300g rump steak | chicken parmi | lamb shanks | chicken schnitzel | pizza

long_description: The Brumby Bar & Grill on Clyde Street is a lively gastropub open nightly from 4pm until midnight, making it one of the latest-closing venues in Jindabyne and a solid apres-ski pick. The menu combines classic pub fare (beer-battered fish and chips, schnitzel, burgers, steak) with a rotating selection of local craft beers. The outdoor area and relaxed vibe make it popular with locals and mountain visitors. Kitchen closes well before midnight – check on arrival.
name: Brumby Bar & Grill
short_description: Gastropub open from 4pm to midnight daily, featuring craft beer, innovative pub fare and a strong local following.
signature_dishes: chicken schnitzel | beer-battered fish and chips | burgers | steak | craft beer selection

address: Shop 3, Level 2, Snowy Mountains Plaza (Old Town Centre), Jindabyne NSW 2627
long_description: Cafe Darya is a beloved Snowy Mountains institution offering authentic Persian cuisine in a cosy, unpretentious setting at the Old Town Centre. Dishes like slow-braised camel with chilli, radish, fennel and chickpeas showcase bold Middle Eastern flavours and local produce. The restaurant is BYO (wine and beer) and cash only – making a trip to the bottle shop and ATM beforehand essential. Open Tuesday–Saturday from 6:30pm in winter, Thursday–Saturday off-season.
name: Cafe Darya
short_description: Authentic Persian restaurant – one of the most distinctive dining experiences in the Snowy Mountains, BYO and cash only.
signature_dishes: slow-braised camel with chilli, radish, fennel and chickpeas | Persian lamb | baghali polo

address: Shop 10C, Nuggets Crossing Shopping Centre / Kosciuszko Road, Jindabyne NSW 2627
long_description: Bacco on Kosciuszko Road is Jindabyne's go-to Italian, serving a broad menu of thin-crust pizzas, house-made pastas, veal scallopini, pollo bacco, affogato and lumberjack cake. It's particularly family-friendly and one of the few places in town open until midnight, making it the best late-night dine-in option. Takeaway pizza and pasta available via a separate phone line. Dine-in is à la carte with BYO wine.
name: Bacco Italian Restaurant
short_description: Family-friendly Italian restaurant open 7 days with dine-in, BYO wine and late-night takeaway pizza and pasta.
signature_dishes: pizzas | pollo bacco | veal scallopini | affogato | lumberjack cake

address: Shop 19, Nuggets Crossing Shopping Centre, 5 Snowy River Avenue, Jindabyne NSW 2627
long_description: Takayama brings Japanese izakaya mountain food to Jindabyne, inspired by the après-ski mountain hut culture of Japan. The menu features edamame, sushi rolls, pork gyoza, karaage chicken, katsu, tataki beef and ramen, complemented by Sapporo beer and yuzu cocktails. The sleek, modern interior seats intimate groups, and the team behind it also runs the town's other quality restaurants. Bookings are strongly recommended in peak ski season.
name: Takayama Restaurant & Bar
short_description: Sleek Japanese izakaya-style restaurant in Nuggets Crossing open Tuesday–Saturday from 5:30pm – Sapporo on tap.
signature_dishes: pork gyoza | karaage chicken | sushi rolls | ramen | Sapporo on tap | yuzu cocktail

cuisine: modern Australian | Asian fusion | fine dining
long_description: Embers Fireside Restaurant at Horizons Lake Jindabyne is the only upscale dining experience in the Snowy Mountains base town. The menu blends modern Australian and Asian influences: karaage chicken, sesame duck, fillet mignon, chilli garlic prawn pasta. Operating Tuesday–Saturday during off-season (October–May) and expanding to full winter hours, the roaring fireplace and lake-view setting make it the destination for date nights and special occasions. Call 02 6456 2562 to book.
name: Embers Fireside Restaurant (Horizons Lake Jindabyne)
short_description: Jindabyne's only premium fine-dining restaurant – Asian-Modern Australian menu with roaring winter fireplace, reservations essential.
signature_dishes: karaage chicken | sesame duck | fillet mignon | chilli garlic prawn pasta

long_description: Cocina Taqueria occupies a cosy upstairs space at 33 Kosciuszko Road and has been reinvigorated under new ownership since November 2024. The menu features tacos, burritos, ceviche, jalapeño poppers and Oaxacan lamb barbacoa, alongside tequila, mezcal and margaritas. With outdoor seating and an upstairs dining area, it's a popular choice for groups. Dinner service runs 7 nights from 5:30pm to 8:30pm.
name: Cocina Taqueria
short_description: Contemporary Mexican restaurant on Kosciuszko Road, under new ownership since 2024, open 7 nights from 5:30pm.
signature_dishes: Oaxacan lamb barbacoa tacos | ceviche | jalapeño poppers | margaritas | mezcal selection

long_description: Holly Go Lightly on Thredbo Terrace is the closest thing Jindabyne has to a proper night-life venue, with a beer garden, DJ sessions through winter and summer, and a menu that leans American-comfort: poutine, fried cheese balls, maple bacon burgers and beef cheeseburgers. The relaxed atmosphere makes it equally good for a quiet afternoon beer or a rowdy post-mountain session. Open from 3pm daily, until 11pm on weekends.
name: Holly Go Lightly
short_description: Locals' favourite bar with beer garden, DJ nights, poutine and maple bacon burgers – open until 11pm Fri/Sat.
signature_dishes: poutine | fried cheese balls | maple bacon burger | beef cheeseburger

address: Level 1, Shop 14/33 Kosciuszko Road, Jindabyne NSW 2627
cuisine: bar food | American | burgers | craft beer
long_description: Jindabyne Emporium occupies a level-1 space on Kosciuszko Road with sweeping Lake Jindabyne views. The happy hour runs daily from 4pm to 6pm ($8 schooners and wines), making it the best-value apres-ski drink in town. The food menu covers burgers, tacos, pork belly nuggets and cheeseburger spring rolls, backed by an extensive independent Australian craft beer list, natural/lo-fi wines and Aussie spirits. The setting is casual and the lake view spectacular at sunset.
name: Jindabyne Emporium
short_description: Lake-view bar and eatery with daily 4–6pm Happy Hour, craft burgers, tacos and the best craft beer and lo-fi wine selection in town.
signature_dishes: cheeseburger spring rolls | pork belly nuggets | burgers | tacos | daily Happy Hour $8 schooners 4–6pm

cuisine: bar food | craft beer | share plates
long_description: Jindabyne Brewing Co is the town's only dedicated craft brewery and taproom, located on Nettin Circuit a short drive from the main strip. Flagship beers include Alpine Red X (dark lager) and Hefe Weiss (German wheat beer). The small kitchen puts out meat skewers, house chips and aioli to complement the pints. The taproom opens from 3pm Wednesday–Friday and noon on weekends, making it an ideal first stop on a non-ski afternoon.
name: Jindabyne Brewing Co
short_description: Independent craft brewery with taproom on Nettin Circuit, open from midday weekends – try the Alpine Red X dark lager.
signature_dishes: Alpine Red X dark lager | Hefe Weiss wheat beer | meat skewers | house chips with aioli

long_description: Panorama Thai on Nettin Circuit offers a reliable, warming Thai menu every evening from 5pm, making it one of the most convenient dinner options in Jindabyne. Standout dishes include massaman beef, chilli basil eggplant and the spicy pad kee mao. The relaxed setting and reasonable prices make it popular with families and ski groups. The same lakeside panorama views as the Panorama Jindabyne motel next door.
name: Panorama Thai
short_description: Thai restaurant on Nettin Circuit open 7 nights from 5pm – go-to for warming massaman curry after a cold day on the mountain.
signature_dishes: massaman beef curry | chilli basil eggplant | pad kee mao (spicy) | Thai iced tea

address: Level 3, Shop 5/3 Kosciuszko Road, Jindabyne NSW 2627
long_description: Beach Burrito Co occupies a level-3 perch on Kosciuszko Road with spectacular Lake Jindabyne views. The menu is reliably casual Mexican – tacos, quesadillas, burritos – with a strong cocktail list of tequilas, margaritas and sangria. The kids' menu includes a DIY taco kit, making it one of the most family-friendly dinner options in town. BYO is not permitted.
name: Beach Burrito Co
short_description: Casual Mexican chain with lake views, kids' DIY taco kits, tequila and margaritas – great for families.
signature_dishes: tacos | burritos | quesadillas | margaritas | kids' DIY taco kit

long_description: Bebita is tucked into a quiet spot on Snowy River Avenue, offering a relaxed alternative to the main strip. The menu covers coffee, fresh juices, salads, nachos, burrito bowls and tacos, with house-baked cheesecakes (mint choc, caramilk, Kit Kat) as the standout desserts. BYO wine and beer are welcome, and an outdoor terrace makes it a pleasant lunch spot in fine weather.
name: Bebita
short_description: Wholesome fresh food cafe in Jindabyne's backstreets serving brunch, nachos, burrito bowls and spectacular cheesecakes.
signature_dishes: mint choc cheesecake | caramilk cheesecake | burrito bowl | nachos

long_description: Stacks Pizza at 1 Kosciuszko Road (inside the Banjo Paterson Inn precinct) is Jindabyne's most accessible pizzeria, offering dine-in, takeaway and by-the-slice options. The menu covers all the classics – ham and pineapple, supreme, meat lovers, chorizo and boscaiola – with the Pontiac potato pizza standing out as the local favourite. BYO wine only.
name: Stacks Pizza
short_description: Casual BYO pizzeria serving dine-in, takeaway and by-the-slice pizza – Pontiac potato pizza is the local favourite.
signature_dishes: Pontiac potato pizza | meat lovers pizza | boscaiola pizza | by-the-slice

address: Shop 18B, Nuggets Crossing Shopping Centre, Snowy River Avenue, Jindabyne NSW 2627
long_description: Pinot's Wine Bar in Nuggets Crossing is Jindabyne's most intimate small bar, offering a carefully curated wine list, craft beers and cocktails alongside sophisticated bar snacks: toasted brioche with ricotta and white anchovies, pumpkin and truffle arancini balls, and a cheese board. The small, cosy space fills quickly in ski season, making it the top recommendation for couples seeking a relaxed but upscale evening out.
name: Pinot's Wine Bar
short_description: Best date-night spot in Jindabyne – intimate wine bar with artisan snacks, craft beer, cocktails and a curated wine list.
signature_dishes: toasted brioche with ricotta and white anchovies | pumpkin and truffle arancini | cheese board

long_description: The Jindabyne Bowling Club on Bay Street punches well above its weight as a family dining destination. The bistro menu covers burgers, prawn cutlets, chicken parmi and steak sandwiches at bowlo prices. An indoor playground keeps children occupied, Thursday trivia nights draw a local crowd, and the courtesy bus means you don't need to drive. A reliable, genuinely affordable option for large groups and families.
name: Jindabyne Bowling Club
short_description: Family-friendly bowling club bistro with indoor playground, Thursday trivia and courtesy bus – best-value family dinner in town.
signature_dishes: chicken parmi | prawn cutlets | steak sandwich | burger

address: Shop 1, Nuggets Crossing Shopping Centre, 6 Kosciuszko Road, Jindabyne NSW 2627
long_description: Woolworths in Nuggets Crossing Shopping Centre is the main supermarket in Jindabyne, stocking all grocery staples, fresh produce, deli items, pre-made meals, ski snacks, wine and beer. Open 7am–9pm every day of the year (closed Christmas Day), it's the essential first stop for self-contained accommodation guests. The extensive ready-meal range is popular for easy weeknight ski dinners. The BWS bottle shop is co-located.
name: Woolworths Jindabyne
short_description: Full-size Woolworths supermarket open 7am–9pm every day – the primary grocery stop for self-catering ski accommodation.

address: Shop 1, Nuggets Crossing Shopping Centre, Kosciuszko Road, Jindabyne NSW 2627
long_description: BWS Jindabyne is the main bottle shop in town, co-located with Woolworths in Nuggets Crossing Shopping Centre. It stocks a wide range of beer (including local craft), wine, spirits and RTDs. Open 9am–8pm Monday–Saturday and 10am–8pm Sunday (closed Christmas Day). For BYO restaurants like Cafe Darya and Bacco, an ATM and BWS trip should be planned before the dinner booking.
name: BWS – Beer Wine Spirits (Nuggets Crossing)
short_description: Bottle shop inside Nuggets Crossing Shopping Centre open 7 days – the primary liquor stop for Jindabyne self-catering guests.

long_description: The Market Jindabyne on Snowy River Avenue is part specialty grocery, part cafe. It serves excellent coffee (matcha, juice included), toasties on local sourdough, pastries and smoothie bowls, while also stocking a curated selection of cured meats, cheeses, honey, preserves, organic fruit and vegetables. The combination of eat-in and take-home produce makes it a great morning stop before the mountain or a lazy afternoon browse.
name: The Market Jindabyne
short_description: Specialty food and coffee shop stocking local produce, cured meats, cheese, honey and artisan groceries plus great coffee.
signature_dishes: sourdough toastie | matcha latte | cured meats platter | artisan cheese selection

cuisine: French country | modern Australian | fine dining
long_description: Crackenback Farm Restaurant is consistently cited as one of the best dining experiences in the entire Snowy Mountains region. The Glenn Murcutt-designed dining room has a soaring cathedral ceiling and a roaring open fireplace in winter. The French country-farmhouse menu is produce-driven, seasonal and complemented by a well-selected wine list. In season it opens for both lunch and dinner; outside ski season, dinner only on selected days. Reservations are essential.
name: Crackenback Farm Restaurant
short_description: Award-winning French country restaurant 5 min from Jindabyne with cathedral ceiling, open fire and the best wine list in the Snowies.
signature_dishes: seasonal French-Australian degustation | country farmhouse menu

long_description: Squires Bar & Bistro is the casual dining and drinking outlet at Horizons Lake Jindabyne, remaining open year-round as a complement to the premium Embers Fireside Restaurant which opens seasonally. The beer garden and Squires Cocktail Bar offer relaxed dining, local beers, cocktails and bistro meals. The lakeside hotel setting and waterfront views make it a popular choice for groups staying at Horizons or passing through.
name: Squires Bar & Bistro (Horizons Lake Jindabyne)
short_description: Hotel bar and bistro at Horizons with beer garden and cocktail bar – open while Embers Fireside Restaurant is closed.
signature_dishes: cocktails | local craft beer | bistro meals

address: Nuggets Crossing Shopping Centre, Jindabyne NSW 2627
long_description: Jindabyne has a local IGA-affiliated grocer in addition to Woolworths, providing a convenient option for top-up grocery shopping. Stocking fresh produce, packaged goods, snacks, drinks and some specialty items, it's useful during peak ski season when Woolworths can be extremely busy. Opening hours are shorter than Woolworths, so check before making a special trip. Location and exact hours should be verified on arrival as the store configuration changes.
name: IGA / Local Grocer (formerly in Nuggets Crossing)
short_description: Local IGA-affiliated grocer in Jindabyne for top-up shopping when Woolworths is closed or too busy.

long_description: The Ampol Foodary on Kosciuszko Road is the practical early-morning stop for ski-day fuel. Open from 6:00am seven days a week, it's one of the first businesses in Jindabyne to open and stocks petrol, diesel, hot drinks, packaged snacks, sandwiches and convenience groceries. Essential for self-contained apartment guests needing to fill the car and grab a quick bite before the mountain run.
name: Ampol Foodary Jindabyne
short_description: Service station with attached convenience store open from 6am – essential for early-morning fuel, snacks and hot drinks before heading to the mountain.
signature_dishes: hot coffee | packaged snacks | fuel (unleaded 91, 95, 98, diesel)

long_description: Metro Petroleum on Kosciuszko Road in East Jindabyne is the second service station in the Jindabyne area, useful for guests staying on the eastern side of the lake at Discovery Parks or Siesta Villa. Open from 6:30am on weekdays and 7:30am weekends, it provides fuel, basic convenience goods and cold drinks. Often cheaper fuel than the main-strip station.
name: Metro Petroleum Jindabyne (East Jindabyne)
short_description: Second fuel and convenience stop in East Jindabyne, handy for Discovery Parks guests heading toward Perisher or Thredbo.
signature_dishes: fuel (diesel, U91, U95, U98) | convenience snacks

long_description: The Bean & Barley is the best-reviewed cafe in Berridale (4.4 Google, 4.0 Tripadvisor) and the practical go-to for breakfast before heading to the slopes. Signature dishes include bacon and eggs, egg rolls, bacon rolls, cheesecake, and mud cake. The cafe has an airy, rustic ambience with outdoor seating, highchairs for kids, and accepts credit cards. Opens at 6:30–7am daily, closes at 2pm — meaning it's not an après-ski option.
name: The Bean & Barley
short_description: Berridale's main all-day cafe, open 7 days with breakfast, brunch, and lunch — charming rustic space with gluten-free options.
signature_dishes: Bacon and eggs | Egg roll | Bacon roll | Cheesecake | Mud cake

long_description: The Berridale Inn is the town's main pub and social hub. The restaurant serves Australian and Asian-influenced food (including pub meals from a $10 budget menu and a full dinner menu). The public bar has darts, Keno, TAB, and big-screen TVs; the lounge bar is family-friendly with a pool table and beer garden. Reviews note comfortable warm ambience and friendly service. Important caveat: the pub posted a Facebook notice of temporary closure due to electrical issues in late 2024 — check current operating status before visiting.
name: Berridale Inn
short_description: The town pub — Australian country bar with a restaurant serving Asian-influenced dishes, open fireplace, TAB, and beer garden.
signature_dishes: Pub burgers | Asian stir-fries | Lime chilli squid

long_description: Meet You Halfway is a small but beloved Berridale institution — a vintage caravan coffee van on the Kosciuszko Road highway strip, now expanded with an adjoining dine-in creative space and art gallery. Run by Fen and Jase, the van is known for outstanding coffee (frequently called the best between Cooma and Jindabyne), Reuben toasties, and warm community atmosphere. Pet-friendly outdoor area. Opens early, making it ideal pre-ski. Closes in the afternoon — not an après option.
name: Meet You Halfway
short_description: Beloved vintage caravan coffee stop on Kosciuszko Road with community creative space, art gallery, and excellent espresso.
signature_dishes: Reuben toastie | Espresso coffee | Baked treats

long_description: Out of Bounds is a wood-fired pizza van run by Anthony Green, a former skier who became Berridale's 2023 NSW Local Business of the Year. The dough is slow-fermented over days; toppings are locally sourced. The van offers two formats: fresh hot pizzas on Friday and Saturday from 5pm (phone orders from 5pm on 0412 867 751), and a heat-to-eat range of vacuum-sealed, oven-cooked pizzas available daily from noon for reheating at your accommodation — practical for groups staying in self-contained properties. Located at 20 Boundary Street per one source; van-based so may move.
name: Out of Bounds Berridale Pizza
short_description: Wood-fired pizza van run by a local legend — fresh pizzas Friday–Saturday from 5pm, heat-to-eat range available daily from noon.
signature_dishes: Wood-fired pizza | Heat-to-eat vacuum-sealed pizza

long_description: The Snowy Vineyard & Microbrewery (now rebranded as Dalgety Brewing Co) is a 1980s tourism landmark located 18 km from Berridale on 255 Werralong Road, Dalgety. Nine craft beers on tap including IPA, stout, and hefeweizen, plus the estate's own wines (shiraz, bubbly, ciders). The outdoor areas include Snowy River frontage, outdoor games, and farm animals. Food covers brunch, lunch, and share platters (antipasto, cheese/meat boards, sweet potato fries, wedges, chicken tacos). Open Wed–Sun. Phone: +61 1300 766 608. Note: this is ~18 km from central Berridale but is listed under Berridale 2628 in tourism directories.
name: Snowy Vineyard & Microbrewery (Dalgety Brewing Co)
short_description: Iconic winery and microbrewery on the Snowy River — nine craft beers on tap, estate wines, share platters, and outdoor dining.
signature_dishes: Craft beer sampler (4 beers) | Ginger cider | Antipasto platter | Sweet potato fries | Ploughman's platter | Cheese and charcuterie board

long_description: The Little Grocer Berridale is a gourmand's destination in a small town. It combines Shut The Gate's cellar door tasting room (cool-climate Tumbarumba and Hilltops wines), a premium providore stocked with artisan cheeses, charcuterie, pâté, fresh local sourdoughs, and Merimbula Lake oysters, plus craft beers and spirits. Build-your-own picnic platters can be enjoyed in the Secret Garden. Fresh produce arrives weekly. Also acts as Berridale's best bottle shop. Open Mon–Sat 10am–6pm, Sun 10am–5pm.
name: The Little Grocer / Shut The Gate Cellar Door
short_description: Gourmet providore, bottle shop, and cellar door wine bar combined — artisan cheeses, sourdough, oysters, craft beer, and local wines.
signature_dishes: Artisan cheese board | Charcuterie platter | Merimbula Lake oysters | Local sourdough | Wine tasting flight | DIY picnic platter

long_description: Berridale Thai Restaurant is listed at 74 Jindabyne Road (same building as the Berridale LPO/Post Office). It appears to be a recent addition to the Berridale dining scene with no Tripadvisor reviews yet and no posted hours. Phone contact available. Inclusion is based on verified Tripadvisor listing with confirmed address and phone; details should be treated with caution until the business is more established.
name: Berridale Thai Restaurant
short_description: Thai restaurant at 74 Jindabyne Road — newly listed, no reviews yet.

address: Lot 3 Southern Cross Drive, Berridale NSW 2628
long_description: The SnowGate Restaurant is the on-site dining option at Snowgate Motel on Southern Cross Drive. It serves an international menu for breakfast and dinner and is one of the few Berridale options with evening meals available, making it relevant for après-ski dining. Open to non-motel guests. The bar is also accessible. Given the motel's ski-season focus, hours are most reliable during the June–September season.
name: SnowGate Restaurant
short_description: Family restaurant inside the Snowgate Motel serving international cuisine for breakfast and dinner — open to non-guests.

long_description: The Southern Cross Motor Inn's 100-seat restaurant is one of the larger dining spaces in Berridale, serving pub-style meals with a bar/lounge and open fireplace. Open to the public, not just motel guests. Practical for groups or families wanting a sit-down dinner after skiing. The bar and fire make it a viable après-ski option in the ski season. No separate menu or hours published online — contact the motel directly.
name: Southern Cross Motor Inn Restaurant
short_description: 100-seat restaurant inside the Southern Cross Motor Inn with bar and open fireplace — open to the public.

long_description: The 19th Hole Berridale is the cafe at Coolamatong Snowy Mountains Country Club (golf club), located just outside central Berridale on the road to Jindabyne. It is listed on Tripadvisor with no reviews as yet. Based on the pattern of Australian club cafes, it likely serves coffee, sandwiches, and basic meals. Included for completeness given limited Berridale food options, but treat hours and offerings as unverified.
name: The 19th Hole Berridale
short_description: Cafe at the Coolamatong Golf Club just outside Berridale — coffee and light meals for golfers and passers-by.

long_description: The IGA on Jindabyne Road is the primary grocery option in Berridale for self-catering ski groups. The store stocks standard supermarket essentials, pantry items, frozen food, and some fresh produce. For groups in self-contained properties — which cover a significant portion of Berridale's accommodation — this is a critical stop. Small-town IGA stores typically operate 7am–7pm Mon–Fri and reduced hours on weekends, though exact Berridale hours are not confirmed online. The IGA is also home to the Berridale LPO (post office) at Shop 6a, 74 Jindabyne Road.
name: IGA Berridale
short_description: The town's main supermarket on Jindabyne Road — essential for self-catering ski groups stocking up before heading to the mountain.

long_description: The service station on the Snowy Mountains Highway through Berridale is an essential practical stop for ski-bound travellers — fuelling up, grabbing snacks, hot drinks, and convenience food before hitting the mountain. The exact operator (United, Caltex, or independent) is unconfirmed online but a fuel station is confirmed operational in town. Provides: petrol, diesel, LP gas, convenience store snacks, hot food/pies (likely), coffee. Open daily, extended hours during ski season likely.
name: Berridale Service Station
short_description: Fuel, convenience snacks, and hot food on the highway — the last servo before Jindabyne heading to the snowfields.
signature_dishes: Hot pies | Coffee | Convenience snacks

long_description: The Berridale Bakery is listed as a nearby establishment in Tripadvisor's local data for Berridale (appearing as 'The Berridale Bakery' near Myack Street). No independent website or phone number has been confirmed. Given Berridale's small size and the existing Bean & Barley cafe, this may operate as a small-scale or part-time operation. Include with caution — verify hours and current operation locally before visiting.
name: The Berridale Bakery
short_description: Local bakery in central Berridale — listed in nearby attraction data but hours and details unconfirmed.

long_description: Open since 2007, The Lott Cafe has built a loyal following with a focus on fresh, local produce and seriously good coffee (Killerbee blend and Single-O Origins). With 419 TripAdvisor reviews, it is comfortably the most-reviewed eatery in town. The Sharp/Soho Street corner location puts it at the heart of the morning ski-day rush. Closes at 2pm, so best visited before hitting the mountain.
name: The Lott Cafe
short_description: Cooma's most-reviewed cafe; sharp espresso, fresh local produce, all-day breakfast.
signature_dishes: all-day breakfast | fresh sandwiches | specialty coffee | seasonal produce dishes

long_description: Kuma Pies is a small artisan bakery tucked towards the southern end of Sharp Street, with a cosy back room warmed by an open fire in winter. The beef and mushroom pie and chicken and leek pie are regularly cited as among the best in NSW. Fresh pastries — cherry Danish, apple turnover, vanilla slice, hazelnut yumpie — are baked on-site daily. A mandatory stop for any Cooma visitor; peak-season queues indicate its cult status. TripAdvisor #1 Bakery in Cooma, 162 reviews.
name: Kuma Pies and Pastries
short_description: Cooma's best bakery; legendary meat pies, flaky pastries, and apple turnovers on Sharp Street.
signature_dishes: beef and mushroom pie | chicken and leek pie | apple turnover | cherry Danish | vanilla slice

long_description: 123 Coffee House sits at 123 Sharp Street and blends classic all-day brunch fare with a selection of Vietnamese dishes, fresh juices, and pre-made sandwiches. It uses ONA Coffee, a respected Canberra specialty roaster. Open 7 days from 7am to 5pm, it's one of the most accessible cafes in Cooma for late-morning après-drive coffee. Vegetarian and vegan options available.
name: 123 Coffee House
short_description: All-day brunch café with Vietnamese dishes, fresh juices, and ONA coffee — open 7 days to 5pm.
signature_dishes: all-day breakfast | Vietnamese dishes | fresh juices | ONA coffee

long_description: Pha's Thai recently moved from Sharp Street to 24 Soho Street in Cooma CBD. It is the most-reviewed Thai restaurant in the region and well regarded for authentic flavours and generous portions. Open Tuesday to Saturday for both lunch and dinner sessions. Closed Sunday and Monday. Online ordering and table bookings available through the website.
name: Pha's Thai
short_description: Popular Thai restaurant on Soho Street; 177 TripAdvisor reviews, lunch and dinner Tue–Sat.
signature_dishes: pad thai | green curry | massaman curry | Thai seafood

long_description: Rose's Lebanese Restaurant on Massie Street is Cooma's most-loved ethnic restaurant, with 283 TripAdvisor reviews and consistent praise for hearty Lebanese and Mediterranean dishes. Open Monday to Saturday for lunch and dinner. The family atmosphere and generous meze platters have built a loyal following among locals and ski-season visitors alike. Closed Sunday.
name: Rose's Lebanese Restaurant
short_description: Beloved Lebanese-Mediterranean restaurant on Massie Street; 283 reviews, Mon–Sat.
signature_dishes: meze platter | Lebanese lamb | falafel | hummus

address: Mt Gladstone Road, Snowy Mountains Highway, Cooma NSW 2630
long_description: Miss Heidi's Austrian Tea House sits just below Mt Gladstone Lookout on the Snowy Mountains Highway, bringing an unexpected slice of alpine Europe to Cooma. Traditional Viennese schnitzel, Austrian pancakes with toppings, strudel, and Sacher torte fill the menu. Open 7 days until 5pm; Friday and Saturday dinner service 6–9pm brings the après-ski feel. With 205 TripAdvisor reviews it is one of the most distinctive dining experiences in the Monaro. Off-street parking available.
name: Miss Heidi's Austrian Tea House
short_description: Alpine Austrian tea house near Mt Gladstone Lookout; schnitzel, strudel, Fri–Sat dinner.
signature_dishes: Viennese schnitzel | Austrian pancakes | apple strudel | Sacher torte

long_description: The Cooma Ex-Services Club on Vale Street is the largest club in the Snowy Monaro region, open 7 days a week from 10am. The in-house bistro serves generous portions at excellent value for money — one of Cooma's most popular dinner spots for ski visitors on a budget. Lunch 11:30am–2pm, dinner Sun–Tue 5–8:30pm and Wed–Sat 5–9pm. Non-members can attend as guests. Conference and function facilities also available.
name: Cooma Ex-Services Club Bistro
short_description: Largest club on the Monaro; affordable bistro meals open 7 days, members and visitors welcome.
signature_dishes: schnitzel | steak | fish and chips | roast of the day

long_description: The Alpine Hotel bistro on Sharp Street is a standout for pub dining in Cooma, with 10 beers on tap, an open fire in cooler months, and a menu that covers classics like steak, schnitzel, and chicken parmi. Lunch 12–2pm, dinner 6–9pm daily. The TripAdvisor-reviewed restaurant arm has 212 reviews and is popular for post-mountain dinners. Secure garage parking for motorcycles and special vehicles.
name: Alpine Hotel Bistro
short_description: Central pub with 10 beers on tap, open fire, and bistro serving 7 days for lunch and dinner.
signature_dishes: steak | chicken parmi | fish and chips | pub classics

address: 59-61 Lambie Street (cnr Sharp & Lambie), Cooma NSW 2630
long_description: The Royal Bistro inside the State Heritage-listed Royal Hotel serves traditional Australian pub meals across multiple dining areas including the historic front verandah and outdoor sections. Open Tuesday to Sunday for lunch (12–2:30pm) and dinner (6–8:30pm). Consistently praised for good food and ice-cold beer in a genuinely historic setting. The front sandstone bar is one of the most atmospheric in the Monaro.
name: Royal Hotel Bistro
short_description: Heritage pub bistro in Cooma's 1858 Royal Hotel; Tue–Sun lunch and dinner.
signature_dishes: steak | pub roast | schnitzel | seasonal specials

long_description: The Cooma Hotel on Massie Street dates to 1862 and is the oldest continuously operating hotel in town. The current operator runs a lively bar open from 11am to late, a bistro with lunch and dinner, and a drive-through bottle shop for convenient post-mountain drinks. With a cinema and function rooms on-site, it is one of Cooma's more complete entertainment venues. 96 TripAdvisor reviews.
name: Cooma Hotel Bar & Bistro
short_description: Oldest continuously operating hotel in Cooma (1862); bar, bistro, and drive-through bottle shop.
signature_dishes: pub meals | schnitzel | steak

long_description: Cooma Indian Restaurant at 171 Sharp Street serves a broad menu spanning South Indian dishes and North Indian tandoori specialities. Open Tuesday to Saturday 11am–9pm and Sunday 12–9pm; closed Monday. A warm, welcoming family restaurant that has become a reliable post-ski dinner option, particularly for those craving spice after a cold mountain day. Takeaway available.
name: Cooma Indian Restaurant
short_description: North and South Indian cuisine on Sharp Street; dine-in and takeaway Tue–Sun.
signature_dishes: butter chicken | lamb rogan josh | chicken tikka masala | dosa

long_description: Cooma Thai occupies the upstairs level of 121 Sharp Street and is the most accessible Thai option for budget diners, rated $ on TripAdvisor. Open 7 days for lunch (11am–2:30pm) and dinner (5–9pm). With 47 TripAdvisor reviews and a reputation for generous portions at low prices, it competes directly with Pha's Thai at a lower price point.
name: Cooma Thai
short_description: Budget Thai restaurant upstairs at 121 Sharp Street; open 7 days for lunch and dinner.
signature_dishes: pad thai | fried rice | green curry | tom yum soup

long_description: Grand Court Chinese Restaurant at Snowstop Village serves a broad Cantonese and Chinese menu daily for lunch and dinner, closing at 10pm — making it one of the later-closing sit-down options in Cooma after a mountain day. Part of a small complex at 38 Sharp Street that also houses Domino's Pizza and KFC. 86 TripAdvisor reviews.
name: Grand Court Chinese Restaurant
short_description: Chinese restaurant in Snowstop Village; open 7 days for lunch and dinner with late closing.
signature_dishes: Cantonese BBQ duck | fried rice | sweet and sour pork | dumplings

long_description: Sandi's Hotbake at 26 Bombala Street is the place to stop for an early-morning fresh loaf or pastry before heading to the mountain. Opening at 6am Monday to Friday and closing at 4pm (Saturdays 6am–2pm), it caters squarely to the pre-dawn ski-day crowd. Located near the Cooma Visitor Centre area. Separate from the similarly-named 'Cooma Original Hotbake' on Sharp Street (which keeps different hours).
name: Sandi's Hotbake
short_description: Early-opening bakery on Bombala Street; fresh bread and pastries from 6am Mon–Sat.
signature_dishes: fresh bread | meat pies | pastries | rolls

long_description: Capital Dial-A-Pizza at 86a Sharp Street is a takeaway-and-delivery-only operation open every evening from 5pm to 11pm. With 191 TripAdvisor reviews and the lowest price band in town ($), it is the most popular post-mountain comfort food option for budget ski groups who don't want to venture out. No dine-in service.
name: Capital Dial-A-Pizza
short_description: Cooma's go-to pizza delivery/takeaway; open 7 days from 5pm to 11pm.
signature_dishes: meat lovers pizza | garlic bread | potato wedges

long_description: McDonald's on Sharp Street in central Cooma operates 24-hour drive-through and is a key practical resource for ski-season travellers who need early breakfast before heading to the mountain or late-night food after a long mountain day. Open 5am–10pm for dining room, 24hr drive-through.
name: McDonald's Cooma
short_description: 24-hour drive-through on Sharp Street; practical early-morning ski-day stop.
signature_dishes: Big Mac | McMuffin | McCafe coffee | nuggets

long_description: Woolworths on Vale Street is the largest supermarket in Cooma, offering full grocery, deli, bakery, liquor (BWS attached), and household supplies. Open 7am to 10pm every day, it is the main provisioning stop for self-catered ski groups before heading up the mountain. Staffed checkout and self-serve options. Fresh food, ready meals, and ski-season provisions.
name: Woolworths Cooma
short_description: Full-service supermarket on Vale Street; open 7am–10pm daily for ski supplies.

long_description: Coles at 85–91 Commissioner Street provides the main alternative grocery option to Woolworths in Cooma, with convenient parking and a full range of fresh food, freezer goods, deli, bakery, and liquor. Standard Coles hours — 7am to 9pm on weekdays and Saturday, 8am to 8pm Sunday. Useful for self-catered groups who need a full shop before heading up to Jindabyne or the resorts.
name: Coles Cooma
short_description: Second major supermarket on Commissioner Street; 7am–9pm Mon–Sat, 8am–8pm Sun.

long_description: BWS (Beer Wine Spirits) at 45–47 Sharp Street is Cooma's most accessible standalone bottle shop for ski season visitors, stocking full range of beers, wines, spirits, and mixers. Adjacent to the main motel strip and café precinct. A key stop for self-catering groups heading to the snowfields.
name: BWS Cooma
short_description: Beer, wine, and spirits bottle shop on Sharp Street; convenient for ski-trip provisioning.

long_description: The Cooma Hotel on Massie Street operates a drive-through bottle shop — the most convenient format for car- and van-based ski visitors who don't want to park and walk. Part of the hotel's broader entertainment offering (bar, bistro, cinema). Open during the hotel's standard trading hours.
name: Cooma Hotel Drive-Through Bottle Shop
short_description: Drive-through bottle shop at Cooma Hotel on Massie Street; convenient for vehicle-based travellers.

long_description: Metro Petroleum at 42 Sharp Street is open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week (5am–11pm listed, but has overnight trade), making it the key late-night fuel stop for ski-season travellers arriving or departing outside business hours. Woolworths Rewards fuel discounts apply. The convenience store carries basic food, drinks, and travel supplies. The Ampol station on Bombala Street advertises Woolworths Rewards discounts at 4c/litre.
name: Metro Petroleum Cooma (24hr fuel)
short_description: 24-hour petrol station with convenience store on Sharp Street; Woolworths Rewards fuel discount.

long_description: Ampol Cooma at 41 Sharp Street is the main branded fuel option on the Snowy Mountains Highway corridor through town. Open 6am–6:30pm weekdays (6am–6pm weekends). Offers Woolworths Rewards card discount of 4c per litre, as mentioned in local traveller reviews. A conventional servo with convenience items — not 24 hours.
name: Ampol Cooma
short_description: Ampol service station on Sharp/Bombala corner; Woolworths Rewards 4c/litre discount.

long_description: Domino's Pizza in Snowstop Village at 32 Sharp Street is a popular group-meal option for self-catered ski parties staying in Cooma motels. Online ordering and delivery available. Open Sunday–Thursday 3–9pm, Friday–Saturday 11am–10pm. The extended Friday and Saturday hours align well with ski-week arrivals.
name: Domino's Pizza Cooma
short_description: Delivery pizza from Snowstop Village; open from 3pm (11am Fri–Sat) until 10pm.
signature_dishes: Pepperoni Lover's | BBQ Meatlovers | garlic bread

long_description: KFC at the Snowstop Village complex covers the fast-food chicken gap in Cooma and is notable for being open until 10pm every day — later than most sit-down restaurants. A practical option for large groups arriving late from the mountain. Dine-in and takeaway.
name: KFC Cooma
short_description: KFC outlet in Snowstop Village on Sharp Street; open 10:30am–10pm daily.
signature_dishes: Original Recipe chicken | Zinger burger | chips | Popcorn Chicken

long_description: CISNE at 100 Sharp Street is a newer addition to the Cooma café scene offering a contemporary menu with Asian-influenced dishes alongside café staples. Listed on TripAdvisor's Café and Asian categories. Open 7 days from 8am to 3pm. A good mid-morning stop for those who miss the early Lott Cafe window or prefer a more modern setting.
name: CISNE
short_description: Modern café on Sharp Street; open 8am–3pm daily with Asian-influenced dishes.
signature_dishes: smashed avo toast | Asian-inspired brunch dishes | specialty coffee

long_description: Coffey's Hotel at 6 Short Street has a distinctive hybrid menu combining classic pub fare with Chinese dishes. Open Wednesday to Sunday from noon to 9pm, it is a quieter alternative to the main-street hotels. 36 TripAdvisor reviews reflect a local following. Good for skiers who want a quieter evening meal off the main drag.
name: Coffey's Hotel
short_description: Neighbourhood pub on Short Street; Chinese pub meals, open Wed–Sun noon to 9pm.
signature_dishes: Chinese pub meals | steak | schnitzel

long_description: Enza Cafe is the go-to warm-up stop before and after visiting Jigokudani Snow Monkey Park. Situated right in front of the trail entrance, it serves a crowd-pleasing menu of ramen (excellent for warming up on cold days), thin-crust pizza with Nagano mushroom toppings, fried chicken, apple hand pies, Shinshu apple soft serve ice cream, and the wildly popular Monkey Marshmallow Latte (hot latte topped with a monkey-shaped marshmallow). Seating is both indoor and outdoor. Winter hours are extended (8:30am) for early-bird monkey watchers and skiers.
name: Enza Cafe
notes: Located 35km / 50 min from central Nagano City. Access: take bus from Yudanaka Station to Snow Monkey Park bus stop. Open daily, all seasons. Ski season (Dec-Mar) extended morning hours are key for skiers who also want to see Snow Monkeys. Average spend: ¥1,000-1,999.
short_description: Popular cafe directly at the Snow Monkey Park trailhead, serving ramen, pizza, apple pie, soft serve, and the iconic Monkey Marshmallow Latte.
signature_dishes: Monkey Marshmallow Latte | Shinshu apple soft serve ice cream | Apple hand pie | Ramen (warming broth) | Nagano mushroom pizza

long_description: Opened in 2022, Yudanaka Brewery Complex U is the most modern food-and-drink destination in the Yudanaka area. The brewery produces original craft beers using local Nagano ingredients and water from Yudanaka's natural springs. The restaurant serves carefully curated Shinshu-focused dishes alongside the house beers. The entire complex is housed in a striking building with ample parking (30 spaces). QR-code menu ordering is available in English — a significant practical advantage. The complex also houses a 2nd-floor day-trip onsen bath facility. A hit with both day-trippers from Nagano City and onsen town visitors looking for something non-traditional.
name: Yudanaka Brewery Complex U
name_local: ゆダナカ ブルワリーコンプレックスU
notes: Closes at 6pm — arrive early. The only establishment in Yudanaka area with QR-code English ordering. Has 30 parking spaces. Also has 2nd-floor day-trip onsen (open same hours). Tabelog listing: https://tabelog.com/en/nagano/A2001/A200104/20026081/
short_description: Contemporary craft brewery and restaurant using Shinshu ingredients and Yudanaka hot spring water, with QR-code ordering in English.
signature_dishes: Yudanaka Onsen craft beer (house-brewed) | Shinshu ingredient seasonal dishes | Local sweets and desserts

long_description: Hakko Yamanouchi (発酵 = fermentation) is a beloved local bar/restaurant that celebrates Nagano's fermentation culture — from miso to sake to pickles. The menu features inventive small plates such as smoked pickles with gorgonzola, ginger-roasted chicken, and vegan-friendly tofu-mushroom dishes alongside an excellent selection of local craft beers, sake, and house cocktails. Staff are friendly and the English menu makes ordering accessible for international visitors. Closed Mondays. Particularly warm in winter when the après-ski crowd fills the cosy wooden interior.
name: Hakko Yamanouchi
notes: #4 restaurant in Yamanouchi-machi on TripAdvisor (68 reviews, 4.6/5). Located 5 min walk from Yudanaka Station along Kaede Street. Staff speak limited English but menu has English translations. Stays open until 11pm, making it one of the later-closing options in town.
short_description: Fermentation-focused dining bar with local craft beers, sake, and creative Shinshu-ingredient small plates — one of the best dining experiences near Yudanaka Station.
signature_dishes: Smoked pickles with gorgonzola | Roast beef (Christmas special) | Vegan tofu-mushroom dish | Local craft beer selection | House cocktails

long_description: GOEN (御苑) blends modern design with traditional Japanese service in its prime location directly across from Yudanaka Station. It serves a wide-ranging menu of Japanese dishes including tempura, sashimi, karaage (fried chicken), omakase sushi rolls, and a distinctive 'soba ramen' fusion dish. The restaurant also serves Western-style food, desserts, and coffee, making it reliably versatile. Available vegan sushi options and some English-speaking staff. Good for families and groups with mixed dietary preferences. Has both ground-floor hall seating and a 2nd-floor dining area with terrace.
name: Japanese Dining GOEN
name_local: ジャパニーズダイニング 御苑
notes: Hours may vary significantly by season — call or check Google Maps before visiting. Has vegan sushi options (explicitly mentioned by reviewer). Located 27 meters from Yudanaka Station. Catering and banquet services available. Bilingual menu makes ordering easy.
short_description: Casual Japanese restaurant directly opposite Yudanaka Station, serving sashimi, tempura, karaage, soba ramen, and sushi — with vegan options.
signature_dishes: Soba ramen | Tempura set (especially nozawana tempura) | Omakase sushi rolls | Karaage | Salmon avocado rolls

long_description: Isami Zushi (いさみ寿司) is a popular neighbourhood sushi restaurant located 185 metres from Yudanaka Station, run by a welcoming older Japanese couple known for their hospitality toward foreign visitors. The menu features fresh nigiri, sashimi, and rolls at reasonable prices. The grilled yellowtail fish head is a standout dish. Open until 11pm — one of the later-closing restaurants in Yudanaka. Vegetarian guests can order tamago (egg) sushi and cucumber rolls. The warm, intimate atmosphere and accommodating hosts make it a favourite for repeat visitors to the area.
name: Isami Zushi
notes: TripAdvisor 4.7/5 from 36 reviews — one of the highest-rated restaurants in Yamanouchi. Phone: 0269-33-2311. Located 185m from Yudanaka Station. Vegetarian: tamago and cucumber rolls available. Cash only — bring yen. Hours consistent across all days per TripAdvisor.
short_description: Family-run sushi restaurant steps from Yudanaka Station, praised for fresh sashimi and generous portions — open until 11pm.
signature_dishes: Grilled yellowtail fish head (buri kabutoyaki) | Fresh nigiri set | Sashimi moriawase | Tamago sushi | Cucumber roll

long_description: Kushidoraku (串道楽 — 'skewer pleasure') is an old-school, wood-interior izakaya near the station that attracts a loyal local crowd and adventurous international visitors. The menu covers yakitori skewers (including unusual options like chicken cartilage, hearts, and wings), gyoza dumplings (celebrated as some of the best in Yudanaka), miso soup, potato croquettes, and various grilled meats. An English picture menu makes ordering accessible. Tatami floor seating with low tables creates an authentic Japanese dining atmosphere. The owner and staff can communicate basic English and have a warm approach to international guests. Staff are flexible with vegetarian requests (will cook dishes without fish).
name: Izakaya Kushidoraku
notes: Reserve in advance especially in peak season (Jan-Mar). TripAdvisor #22 of 153 Yamanouchi restaurants. Open very late (midnight) — one of the few options for late-night dining. Smoking permitted inside (check current ventilation). The owner can occasionally be brusque on busy nights — persevere. Staff said to cook vegetarian dishes without fish when asked.
short_description: Authentic Japanese yakitori and barbecue izakaya with picture English menu, cosy tatami seating, and some of the best gyoza in Yudanaka.
signature_dishes: Gyoza (pan-fried dumplings) | Chicken skewers (yakitori moriawase) | Potato croquette (korokke) | Chicken wings on skewer | Shishamo (smelt fish)

long_description: Asashinaya Shokudo is the classic neighbourhood Japanese diner (食堂 = shokudo) in Yudanaka. The menu covers all the bases: ramen (¥700-800), soba, tonkatsu (pork cutlet), tempura, karaage, udon, and curry — classic everyday Japanese fare. The owner-operator is consistently praised for warmth and efficiency. An English picture menu with photos and descriptions makes ordering easy. Particularly popular for families and groups with mixed tastes. Ramen and gyoza are highlights. Located a 10-15 minute walk from Yudanaka Station with roadside parking. The owner sometimes gives out small souvenirs to guests on departure.
name: Asashinaya Shokudo
notes: Hours not listed online — call ahead or check Google Maps. Located ~10-15 min walk from Yudanaka Station. Has parking. Vegetarian: tempura tofu-miso broth dish available when requested. Has been serving the Yudanaka area for many years. TripAdvisor #21 of 153 (4.3/5). Recommended by multiple local ryokan owners to guests.
short_description: Friendly family-run shokudo (casual diner) serving a broad Japanese menu including ramen, soba, tempura, tonkatsu and gyoza — with English picture menu.
signature_dishes: Ramen (¥700-800) | Gyoza | Tempura set (especially macha salt) | Tonkatsu | Soba

long_description: Sobadokoro Yariya is a straightforward, affordable soba restaurant in the Yudanaka area serving classic Shinshu-style buckwheat noodles, both cold (zaru soba) and hot (kake soba). The menu also extends to karaage (fried chicken), fresh apple with each meal, and roast soba tea. For adventurous visitors, basashi (horse meat sashimi) is available — a Nagano specialty. All meals are accompanied by a fresh Shinshu apple. The restaurant is cash-only and does not accept any electronic payments. Open until 11pm daily which is later than most Yudanaka establishments.
name: Soba Dokoro Yariya
notes: Cash only — no card, no electronic money, no QR code. Average spend under ¥999. Located 1.6km from Yudanaka Station (20 min walk or short drive). Hours per Tabelog: 11:00-23:00 daily. All meals served with fresh apple and roast soba tea. Roast soba tea for purchase to take home.
short_description: Casual soba house near Yudanaka with cold and hot Shinshu buckwheat noodles, horse meat sashimi (basashi), and housemade karaage — open until 11pm, cash only.
signature_dishes: Zaru soba (cold buckwheat noodles) | Kake soba (hot broth soba) | Karaage (fried chicken) | Basashi (horse meat sashimi) | Oyaki (buckwheat buns, vegetable-stuffed)

long_description: Chanko Tamaya is a fun, thematic dining experience — a sumo-themed restaurant decorated with sumo photographs and artifacts, located just 2 minutes on foot from Yudanaka Station. The signature dish is chanko-nabe (ちゃんこ鍋), the highly nutritious stew traditionally served at sumo stables that includes chicken, vegetables, tofu, and other ingredients in a rich broth. The menu also includes yakitori, minced crab dumplings, and grilled pork. Capacity of 35 seats (30 floor seating, 5 chairs). No reservations required. Closed Wednesdays.
name: Chanko Tamaya
name_local: ちゃんこ料理 たまや
notes: 2 min walk from Yudanaka Station main exit. Closed Wednesdays and Dec 31/Jan 1. Average spend ¥2,000-3,000. Dinner only (evenings). Sumo-themed decor is a fun novelty. Cash only likely — confirm at time of visit.
short_description: Sumo-themed restaurant steps from Yudanaka Station, specialising in chanko-nabe (sumo stew) with yakitori and grilled meats.
signature_dishes: Chanko-nabe (sumo hot pot stew) | Yakitori (chicken skewers) | Minced crab dumplings | Grilled pork

long_description: D-Line is a retro-vibed bar-cafe in a distinctive building right next to Yudanaka Station. Known for an eclectic interior aesthetic, excellent Japanese whisky selection (including premium Scotch and domestic labels), cocktails, and simple food including pizza. Open from 6pm nightly, it's the closest thing Yudanaka has to a dedicated après-ski bar. Popular with international visitors and ski-season workers. The pizza is consistently praised. Closed Thursdays.
name: D-Line Kitchen & Bar
notes: 87 metres from Yudanaka Station. Closed Thursdays. Evening only. One of the very few places in Yudanaka open past 10pm. Japanese whisky selection is notably good — ask the bartender for recommendations. Retro 'Shining'-esque decor has cult following.
short_description: Quirky retro pub/cafe 1 minute from Yudanaka Station with pizza, cocktails, Japanese whisky, and late-night après-ski atmosphere.
signature_dishes: Pizza | Japanese whisky selection | House cocktails | Draft beer

long_description: Sekiei Drive-In is a local legend — a classic Japanese cafeteria-style diner that has been serving Yudanaka since its opening on March 5, 1967. The menu covers standard Japanese comfort food. The drive-in format and large portions make it popular with families and groups. Limited to lunch and dinner service (closed Sundays and Mondays based on current schedule). An 8-minute walk from Yudanaka Station. Expect Japanese-language menus and minimal English service.
name: Sekiei Drive-In
notes: Opened 1967. Closed Sun-Mon. Last order 20:00 (8pm) — closes early. Cash only. 8 min walk from Yudanaka Station (461m). Limited English — pointing at menu or translating photos recommended.
short_description: Old-school Japanese drive-in diner near Yudanaka with lunch and dinner service — a local institution since 1967.
signature_dishes: Japanese set meals (teishoku) | Seasonal Japanese specials

long_description: Ichidaya is an intimate local izakaya near Yudanaka Station known for its simple, honest grilled food and neighbourhood charm. The menu focuses on yakitori (chicken skewers), shishamo (smelt fish), grilled squid, and other classic izakaya staples. The small space and tatami seating create a genuinely local feeling, making it popular with ski and snowboard workers as well as Japanese guests. Limited English.
name: Ichidaya
notes: TripAdvisor rated 4.6/5 (12 reviews). Cosy local gem. Limited hours — call ahead. Cash only. Primarily Japanese-speaking — bring a translation app. Reservations recommended in peak season.
short_description: Cosy local izakaya with yakitori, shishamo, grilled squid, and a welcoming neighbourhood atmosphere.
signature_dishes: Yakitori set | Shishamo (grilled smelt) | Grilled squid | Chicken heart skewer

long_description: Shimaya Soba is the dining operation associated with Shimaya Ryokan in central Yudanaka, specialising in handmade Shinshu soba (信州そば). Shinshu-style soba uses locally grown buckwheat and is typically served cold (zaru) or hot. Accompaniments include nozawana pickles, tofu, and seasonal mountain vegetables. The soba is made fresh daily from high-quality buckwheat flour. Note that this is a separate establishment from the ryokan's room accommodation — the restaurant is open to non-guests.
name: Shimaya Soba
notes: Part of Shimaya Ryokan complex. Open to non-guests. Hours vary — contact via ryokan website or by phone. Cash only. Soba is made fresh daily in limited quantities — go early to avoid sell-out.
short_description: Traditional Shinshu soba restaurant connected with Shimaya ryokan, serving handmade buckwheat noodles with local Nagano sides.
signature_dishes: Zaru soba (cold handmade Shinshu buckwheat noodles) | Kake soba (hot broth soba) | Soba set with nozawana pickles | Tofu dishes

long_description: Dohshokan (道松館) is a local traditional Japanese restaurant in Yudanaka Onsen that serves classic Shinshu regional cuisine. The menu centres on locally foraged mountain vegetables (sansai), Chikuma river fish, handmade soba, and other Nagano staples. The atmosphere is traditional and unhurried — a good representation of rural Japanese dining culture. Limited English, but the proprietors are welcoming to international guests who make the effort to visit.
name: Dohshokan
notes: Data is limited — confirm hours by phone or in person before visiting. Cash only expected. A genuine local establishment, not tourism-facing. Best visited with some Japanese language capability or a translation app.
short_description: Traditional Japanese restaurant in Yudanaka offering local Shinshu cuisine including soba, seasonal mountain vegetables, and river fish.
signature_dishes: Shinshu soba | Sansai (wild mountain vegetables) dishes | River fish from Chikuma River | Local seasonal set meals

long_description: Tamagawa is a long-standing handmade soba restaurant in the quaint Shibu Onsen village, about 1km uphill from Yudanaka. Each morning the family prepares by hand only enough soba for the day — once it's sold out, they close. Signature items are zaru soba (plain cold noodles), tororo soba (with grated mountain yam), and kurumidare soba (with walnut sauce, a Nagano regional specialty). The soba soft serve ice cream is only available to guests who order noodles. Limited seating. Smoking prohibited.
name: Tamagawa Soba (Shibu Onsen)
name_local: 手打ちそば うどん 玉川
notes: Located in Shibu Onsen — 20 min walk uphill from Yudanaka Station (or short taxi/bus ride). Closes when daily soba supply runs out — arrive early at lunch. No smoking. Soba soft serve only for soba-ordering customers. Vegetarian-friendly as soba broth can be made without fish stock on request.
short_description: Handmade soba and udon restaurant in Shibu Onsen with three signature styles: zaru, tororo, and kurumidare (walnut sauce soba) — only daily-made quantities available.
signature_dishes: Kurumidare soba (walnut sauce buckwheat noodles) | Tororo soba (grated yam on soba) | Zaru soba (cold handmade buckwheat) | Soba soft serve ice cream (with soba order only)

long_description: Snow Monkey Beer Live is an annual craft beer festival held on the slopes of Shiga Kogen in mid-March, combining Japanese microbrewery beers with live music performances. The event celebrates the end of ski season with a festival atmosphere on the mountain, and typically draws visitors from across Japan and internationally. Tickets and timing vary year-to-year — check the official website for current season dates. The event is a highlight of the Japanese ski social calendar.
name: Snow Monkey Beer Live
name_local: スノーモンキービアライブ
notes: Annual event — mid-March typically. Check http://snowmonkey.jp/ for current year dates and ticket booking. Held at Shiga Kogen ski resort (not Yudanaka town itself, but a major regional event). Times vary by day. A must-attend for ski/craft beer enthusiasts.
short_description: Annual craft beer and live music festival on the Shiga Kogen ski slopes in mid-March — a bucket-list après-ski event.
signature_dishes: Japanese craft beer selection (multiple breweries) | Festival food stalls

long_description: Eiraku (永楽 — 'eternal prosperity') is a no-frills Chinese-Japanese restaurant that has served the Yudanaka community for decades. The menu features classic Japanese Chinese-style food: ramen, gyoza, fried rice, and Chinese-influenced set meals. Counter seating with a local, unpretentious atmosphere. Widely recommended for its small ramen and gyoza combo — very filling and very cheap. The language barrier is real, but pointing at simple menu items works fine.
name: Chinese Food Eiraku
notes: Very cheap and filling — ideal for budget travellers. Counter seating, very local. Hours unknown — check Google Maps before going. Cash only. No English menu.
short_description: Long-standing Chinese-Japanese restaurant near Yudanaka offering ramen, gyoza, and Japanese-Chinese comfort food at very low prices.
signature_dishes: Ramen | Gyoza | Fried rice

long_description: Tofuya (豆腐屋 — 'tofu shop/restaurant') is a traditional establishment in Yudanaka area that specialises in handmade Shinshu-style tofu (豆腐), including hiyayakko (cold fresh tofu), agedashi dofu (deep-fried tofu in broth), yudofu (hot pot tofu), and dengaku tofu (grilled tofu with miso). Shinshu tofu is noted for its richness owing to the quality of regional mountain water and locally grown soybeans. The restaurant's dishes are simple, wholesome, and represent an important vein of Nagano traditional cuisine. Vegetarian-friendly relative to most local options.
name: Tofuya
notes: Note: Tofuya in Yudanaka is NOT the same as the famous 'Tofuya Ukai' luxury chain in Tokyo/Kawasaki. This is a small local Yudanaka tofu restaurant. Hours and specific address unconfirmed — verify directly. Tofu broth may contain fish-based dashi — ask if vegetarian.
short_description: Traditional tofu-focused restaurant in Yudanaka serving fresh handmade Shinshu tofu dishes and local seasonal accompaniments.
signature_dishes: Hiyayakko (cold fresh tofu) | Agedashi tofu (deep-fried in broth) | Yudofu (hot pot tofu) | Dengaku tofu (grilled with miso)

long_description: The Lawson convenience store at Yudanaka Station is an essential stop for all travellers in the area. For skiers, it is the place to grab breakfast before the mountain bus, quick lunches, energy bars, hot coffee, nikuman (steamed meat buns), onigiri (rice balls), and snacks. The ATM inside accepts international cards (VISA/Mastercard) — critical in this largely cash-based town. Open hours may vary from the standard 24-hour format for rural locations. Stock also includes sandwiches, bento boxes, noodle cups, desserts, sauces, and basic toiletries. Children's snacks and drinks available.
name: Lawson (Yudanaka Ekimae)
name_local: ローソン 湯田中駅前店
notes: 87m from Yudanaka Station. ATM accepts international Visa/Mastercard — important for cash in this area. Not confirmed 24-hour in this rural location — check hours on Google Maps before counting on late-night access. Take-out only format. Tabelog category: Convenience store.
short_description: Essential convenience store (konbini) 87 metres from Yudanaka Station — onigiri, bento, hot foods, ATM (accepts foreign cards), ski essentials.
signature_dishes: Onigiri (rice balls, multiple fillings) | Nikuman (steamed pork bun) | Hot coffee (from machine) | Bento boxes | Sake cup noodles / ramen

long_description: The 7-Eleven in the Sano district of Yamanouchi is situated on Route 292 (Joshinetsu Expressway spur), making it the primary convenience store for travellers driving toward Snow Monkey Park, Ryuoo Ski Area, or Shiga Kogen. Stock includes standard konbini fare: hot foods, coffee, onigiri, sandwiches, snacks, drinks, basic medicines, and convenience items. ATM service available (may accept international cards). Hotarutei Villas notes this store as 5 minutes by car from their property.
name: 7-Eleven Yamanouchi Sano
name_local: セブン-イレブン 山ノ内町佐野店
notes: 722m from Yudanaka Station. On Route 292 — key stop for drivers. Hours likely not 24hr in this rural area — check Google Maps. Important for Hotarutei Villas guests (5 min drive). The nearest 7-Eleven for many Kanbayashi-area accommodations.
short_description: The 7-Eleven on Route 292 in Sano — critical konbini for drivers headed to Snow Monkey Park, Ryuoo ski area, or Shiga Kogen.
signature_dishes: Onigiri | Hot coffee (Seven Café brand) | Bento boxes | Hot snacks (oden, nikuman)

address: Nakano City / Yamanouchi area, Nagano (multiple branches)
long_description: Tsuruya is the premium supermarket chain of Nagano Prefecture, beloved by both locals and savvy visitors for its exceptional selection of local Shinshu products, fresh produce, and prepared foods. A Tsuruya stop is a highlight for food-curious travellers: look for Shinshu apples in season (September-November), locally milled soba flour, hand-fermented miso, nozawana pickles, walnut sauce, local sake, and the chain's own excellent prepared foods and bakery products. The nearest large Tsuruya branches are in Nakano City or Yamanouchi area — approximately 15-20 minutes' drive from central Yudanaka. The Ippongi Park area has a branch.
name: Tsuruya Supermarket (Nakano / Yamanouchi Branch)
notes: Hotarutei Villas staff recommend Tsuruya Ippongi (10 min by car) or AEON Nakano (10 min by car) for full grocery shopping. Tsuruya own-brand products make excellent souvenirs — particularly the apple products and soba. Accepts cards at most branches. Hours approximately 9am-9pm.
short_description: Nagano's beloved regional supermarket chain with outstanding local produce — Shinshu apples, miso, soba, nozawana, sake, and the famous Tsuruya original products.
signature_dishes: Shinshu apples (seasonal) | Shinshu soba (fresh and dried) | Local miso varieties | Nozawana pickles | Walnut sauce (kurumi dare) | Local Nagano sake

long_description: Mikasa is a small neighbourhood cafe near Yudanaka Station, serving standard Japanese cafe fare — coffee, tea, soft drinks, light meals, and desserts. A quiet spot to warm up between activities. Limited English but standard pointing-at-menu service works. Cash likely expected.
name: Mikasa
notes: Limited data available. Primarily a local hangout. Best for coffee and light snacks rather than a full meal. Verify hours before visiting.
short_description: Small local cafe in Yudanaka serving coffee, tea, light meals and desserts.
signature_dishes: Coffee | Japanese set lunch | Cake

long_description: For serious food experiences in Yudanaka, the in-house kaiseki (懐石) dinners at the premium ryokan — particularly Yorozuya, Kambayashi Hotel Senjukaku, Hotel Issa-tei/Biyu no Yado, Tawaraya, and Aburaya Tousen — represent the pinnacle of local Shinshu cuisine. A typical winter kaiseki at these properties includes: sakizuke (small starter), hassun (seasonal platter), yakimono (grilled Shinshu beef or river fish), mushimono (steamed dish), simmered mountain vegetables, rice with local pickles (nozawana, shinshuu miso), miso soup, and dessert (often apple compote or matcha sweet). Most are served in private dining rooms or at low traditional tables. Reservations are part of the booking process for ryokan stays; some accept outside guests for dinner (call ahead).
name: Ryokan Kaiseki Dining (In-House)
notes: This is a category entry for the in-house ryokan dining experience. Top ryokan for kaiseki: Yorozuya ($$$$), Kambayashi Senjukaku ($$$$), Biyu no Yado ($$$), Tawaraya ($$$). Most accommodate dietary restrictions with 24hr advance notice. Some properties (Senjukaku) accept non-guests for dinner — call ahead. Kaiseki at these properties is ¥5,000-15,000/person typically.
short_description: The highest-quality dining in Yudanaka happens inside ryokan dining rooms — kaiseki multi-course meals featuring Shinshu beef, river fish, sansai, and local seasonal produce.
signature_dishes: Shinshu beef (Wagyu-style regional beef) | River fish (iwana, yamame — Chikuma River trout/char) | Sansai (wild mountain vegetables — fiddleheads, butterbur, etc.) | Nozawana pickles | Mushroom dishes (shimeji, matsutake in season) | Miso soup with local tofu | Apple dessert (Shinshu apple)

long_description: Chokkun is a local neighbourhood izakaya and dining bar that spans several categories — izakaya, dining bar, and ramen. It's a laid-back spot for local workers and the occasional international visitor looking for inexpensive Japanese food and drinks. Notably, it accepts QR code payments (PayPay etc.) but not credit cards — useful for visitors with Japanese payment apps.
name: Chokkun
notes: 1.8km from Yudanaka Station (20 min walk). Accepts QR code payments (PayPay), but not credit cards. Average spend ¥1,500. Hours and closing days not confirmed — verify before visiting.
short_description: Local izakaya-dining bar with ramen, draft beer, and izakaya fare — QR payment accepted.
signature_dishes: Ramen | Draft beer | Izakaya snacks

address: Various locations — Yudanaka, Shibu Onsen, Snow Monkey Park trail
long_description: Oyaki (おやき) are a defining Nagano street food — dough parcels (from wheat, buckwheat, or millet) stuffed with fillings including nozawana (pickled greens), kabocha squash, red bean paste, eggplant miso, or mushroom. They are steamed or baked and served warm. Look for oyaki at Enza Cafe (near Snow Monkey Park), at the Tsuruya supermarket, and occasionally at small stalls in the Yudanaka/Shibu Onsen area. Shinshu apple products — fresh juice, apple pie, apple soft serve, and apple jam — are available at Enza Cafe and various convenience stores. These foods represent the most accessible and affordable local Nagano specialties.
name: Oyaki and Shinshu Street Food (Various Vendors)
name_local: おやき・信州郷土料理
notes: Best oyaki at Enza Cafe (buckwheat buns), Tsuruya supermarket, and roadside stalls. Nozawana and vegetable fillings are vegetarian. Red bean filling is vegan. Ask about dashi in broth-based dishes. Apple products are best in autumn (Sep-Nov) but available year-round as processed goods.
short_description: Look for oyaki (stuffed buckwheat dumplings), Shinshu apple products, and local food vendors in and around Yudanaka and on the Snow Monkey Park trail.
signature_dishes: Oyaki with nozawana filling | Oyaki with kabocha (squash) filling | Oyaki with red bean (anko) filling | Shinshu apple pie | Apple soft serve (Shinshu apple)

long_description: Tamagawa Honten is arguably the most important standalone restaurant in Shibu Onsen. Set kitty-corner from the #2 public bath (Sasa-no-yu), it has served hand-milled buckwheat soba for decades. The soba flour is ground from Shinshu-contracted buckwheat using a stone mill on-site each morning; only the day's amount is made, so the restaurant closes when sold out. Zaru-soba (cold, with dipping broth) shows the noodles at their purest. Tororo-soba (with grated yam) and kurumidare-soba (walnut sauce) are house specialties. The soba soft-serve ice cream — only available if you've ordered soba — is a cult item. Lunch service only; closes by early afternoon. The rare establishment in Shibu that accepts major credit cards.
name: Tamagawa Honten
name_local: 手打蕎麦うどん 玉川本店
short_description: The definitive soba restaurant of Shibu Onsen — hand-ground Shinshu buckwheat, stone-milled fresh each morning, served beside the Sasa-no-yu bathhouse.
signature_dishes: Zaru soba (cold buckwheat noodles) | Tororo soba (with grated yam) | Kurumidare soba (walnut dipping sauce) | Soba soft-serve ice cream (must order soba first)

hours.note: Hours vary seasonally; closes when sold out. Confirm before visiting.
long_description: Yariya is the second soba option in Shibu Onsen and offers a slightly warmer, more eccentric dining room — filled with miniatures and memorabilia, run by a local family. The soba is well-regarded by visitors passing through for the snow monkeys or the kuyu meguri. Karaage (Japanese fried chicken) is a popular side order. Tends to be busy at lunch; small seating capacity means waits are common on busy days. Cash only. No advance reservations accepted. Hours are lunch-only; confirm locally as they change seasonally.
name: Soba Dokoro Yariya
short_description: Cosy and homely soba shop on the main cobblestone street — the alternative to Tamagawa, with a family atmosphere and karaage alongside noodles.
signature_dishes: Handmade soba | Karaage (fried chicken)

hours.note: Irregular hours. Queue forms before opening. Confirm locally.
long_description: Chokkun is the most beloved eating destination in Shibu Onsen among international visitors, and its appeal has nothing to do with a menu — because there is no menu. The host (and often his partner) cooks an omakase sequence of whatever inspires him that evening: local fish, seasonal vegetables, tofu, mushrooms, sometimes ramen. Prices are remarkably low (around ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person including drinks). The sign on the door says 'come meet the funny owner'. Beer is sometimes poured by guests themselves from taps behind the counter. A polaroid wall tracks visitors from around the world. Vegetarian guests have been accommodated when they told the owner in advance. The single most important social spot in the village. Cash only; QR code payments accepted. Opens around 18:00–18:30.
name: Izakaya Chokkun
name_local: 居酒屋 ちょっくん
short_description: No-menu omakase izakaya — Shibu Onsen's Midnight Diner. The charismatic host cooks what he feels like; the result is always generous and often unforgettable.
signature_dishes: Nightly omakase (chef's choice, no fixed menu) | Local sake selection | Draft beer (sometimes self-serve)

long_description: Tokumi might look closed from the outside, but venture in and you'll find a small counter-seating ramen shop that feels very local and very authentic. The menu is limited — ramen, gyoza, oyako-don, a few sides — but it's cheap, filling, and warming after a cold day's bathing. An English menu exists, which is a pleasant surprise. The late closing time (midnight on weekdays and weekends) makes this the de facto last-resort dinner option in a village that largely closes by 21:00. Closes Tuesday. Noted to serve alcohol.
name: Ramen Tokumi
short_description: Shibu Onsen's no-frills ramen shop — cheap, warming, counter seating, and one of the only places open for both lunch and late dinner.
signature_dishes: Ramen (local Shinshu-style broth) | Gyoza | Oyako-don (chicken and egg rice bowl)

hours.note: Hours not consistently published. Reservations via TableCheck recommended. Confirm before visiting.
long_description: Gonki occupies a remarkable niche in Shibu Onsen: a French-inspired small restaurant and wine bar that uses local Yamanouchi produce — mountain vegetables, river fish, wild game — to create dishes that feel more Burgundy than Nagano while remaining entirely rooted in their valley.
